title: CASE OF NIKOLIĆ v. SERBIA
conclusion: Violation of Article 3 - Prohibition of torture (Article 3 - Effective investigation) (Procedural aspect)
summary: In the case of Nikolić v. Serbia, the applicant, Mr. Matija Nikolić, a Serbian national of Roma origin represented by the European Roma Rights Centre, brought a complaint against the Republic of Serbia. The case highlighted the vulnerability of Roma and Traveller children to police ill-treatment and the systemic failures in investigating such allegations. On 16 November 2012, when Mr. Nikolić was a minor, he was questioned by police at the Bački Petrovac Police Station regarding alleged thefts. He alleged that officers kicked him in the stomach and hit him in the head, causing him to lose consciousness and requiring emergency surgery for an incarcerated hernia. Despite his detailed complaint and the seriousness of his injuries, the initial investigation was conducted by the same police station implicated in the alleged abuse, and significant delays and procedural shortcomings followed. The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights, which prohibits torture and inhuman or degrading treatment. While the Court found insufficient evidence to establish that Mr. Nikolić’s injuries were caused by police ill-treatment, it ruled that the investigation was neither prompt nor independent, violating the procedural aspect of Article 3. This judgment is significant as it underscores the persistent barriers Roma and Traveller individuals face in accessing justice, particularly in cases involving alleged police misconduct—a concern rooted in a long history of discrimination across Europe.
